evals.prompt: Do 5 replies to posts from AI agent builders.
evals.expected_output: Selects task mode, runs preflight, creates one materialized reply task with count 5, follows its exact task blueprint through automatic discovery and draft generation, then presents the returned content reviews.
expectations: Uses tw task create with surface reply and count 5
Does not invoke twitter-automation
Requires the returned task_blueprint_ref and does not require a task-proposal review_ref
Uses tw task show only for that exact blueprint until drafts or a terminal shortfall/failure
Authorizes no reply mutation before per-draft content approval

evals.prompt: 帮我回复 3 条讨论 AI 编程工具的帖子。
evals.expected_output: Uses Simplified Chinese interface text, preserves the direction, and asks the user to choose a discovery count from 5 through 10 before invoking tw.
expectations: Does not invoke tw with count 3
Explains that discovery tasks require a count from 5 through 10
Keeps commands and refs in English
Does not invent exact targets

evals.prompt: Reply to https://x.com/example/status/1234567890123456789 with exactly: Thanks for sharing — this is useful.
evals.expected_output: Selects exact-action mode, preserves the target/text pair, runs a dry-run, displays both, and waits for explicit approval before one dispatch.
expectations: Uses tw action reply with --dry-run
Preserves the exact reply punctuation
Never treats task creation or deterministic source selection as mutation approval

evals.prompt: Reply to 10 startup posts.
evals.expected_output: Selects task mode, runs preflight, creates one materialized reply task with count 10, and follows its exact task blueprint until automatic discovery and generation produce content reviews or a terminal result.
expectations: Uses tw task create with surface reply and count 10
Creates one task rather than auto-chunking
Does not stop because task create omits review_ref
Does not schedule or send replies before content approval

evals.prompt: Approve all five replies.
evals.expected_output: Refuses broad batch mutation approval, presents all current content reviews together as a numbered set, and requests one explicit decision per exact review ref.
expectations: Displays all current content reviews instead of forcing one-at-a-time reveal
Does not invent a task or source approval stage
Does not collapse independent review refs
Authorizes no more than one mutation per content approval

evals.prompt: Reply 'nice work' to that tweet we looked at earlier.
evals.expected_output: Asks for an exact target or a bounded discovery direction and never infers the target from history or browser state.
expectations: Does not run exact-action mode without one exact target
Does not infer browser state
Asks one concise clarification

evals.prompt: The manual reply task now shows five draft artifacts. Show me all five so I can decide on each one.
evals.expected_output: Inspects every exact artifact returned by the task, follows each artifact's pending content review, and presents all five drafts together with numbered target, reply text, and review refs.
expectations: Runs tw draft show only for the five exact artifact refs returned by task show
Displays all five pending content reviews in one numbered set
Includes the exact target, reply text, and review ref for every draft
Accepts a per-item decision map and leaves omitted items pending
Does not accept approve all as batch mutation authority

evals.prompt: These five candidates are wrong. Redo it and search for the exact phrase let's connect instead.
evals.expected_output: Shows every pending content review from the old automatic batch and asks the user to confirm skipping them. After confirmation it skips those reviews, reruns preflight, and creates one fresh five-reply task with the new exact direction.
expectations: Does not use task review or source review commands
Skips every confirmed still-pending content review and verifies status skipped
Keeps the historical task and drafts recorded
Reruns mandatory preflight because a fresh task is a new preflight boundary
Creates one fresh task with the latest direction and the original count
Does not transfer old content authority or authorize an X mutation

evals.prompt: Approve all five targets you just showed me.
evals.expected_output: Explains that new manual tasks do not have target-approval reviews and that approving all cannot authorize five reply mutations. It displays the generated drafts and asks for one explicit decision per content review.
expectations: Does not invoke tw task review
Does not reinterpret target approval as content approval
Requires one explicit decision per exact draft review
Schedules no X mutation from approve all

evals.prompt: The exact-reply dry-run passed earlier in this session. I approve the unchanged target and reply you just displayed.
evals.expected_output: Reuses the current exact-action flow's preflight result and dispatches the exact unchanged target/reply pair once without another update or preflight fetch.
expectations: Does not rerun preflight for the exact unchanged approval
Requires the same target, text, and dry-run scope
Dispatches once and stops on unknown evidence

evals.prompt: Find 11 reply targets about startup distribution.
evals.expected_output: Stops before invoking tw and asks the user to choose a discovery count from 5 through 10 without silently splitting the request.
expectations: Does not invoke tw with count 11
Enforces the upper discovery limit of 10
Does not auto-chunk or infer targets

evals.prompt: I created the reply task. Its exact task still says awaiting_selection after 105 seconds, then returns draft_status pending_review before the 15-minute deadline. Continue it.
evals.expected_output: Keeps polling only the exact task blueprint within the fixed deadline, does not report a false block after 105 seconds, and follows every exact artifact ref when pending_review appears.
expectations: Runs tw task show only with the exact returned task_blueprint_ref
Uses tw draft show for every exact artifact ref returned by that task
Never searches a global task or review list
Stops as contract drift if the new manual task creates source reviews

evals.prompt: Retry #5. The current task shows its unchanged target and reply, and the durable result is action_preparation_failed with reply:blocked_before_dispatch, no dispatched_at, and confirmation_state not_required.
evals.expected_output: Treats the old reply as conclusively not sent, reruns preflight, and creates a fresh exact-action dry-run from the same exact target/text without reopening the old scheduled mutation. It displays the fresh dry-run and waits for explicit approval before one dispatch.
expectations: Does not treat ActionRecord or EvidenceRecord counts as proof of dispatch
Does not execute or reschedule the failed scheduled task
Uses the exact unchanged target and reply from the current task
Runs a fresh exact-action dry-run and requires fresh explicit approval
Still refuses retries for unknown, post-dispatch, confirmed, or inconclusive outcomes

evals.prompt: I approved the reply drafts. They are all scheduled now, so keep watching and tell me which ones actually send.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the session active, polls each exact returned scheduled-task ref, and repeatedly reports every original draft number under Sent, Not sent yet, or Needs attention. It reads scheduler evidence when each leaves scheduled/running and reports final per-reply outcomes instead of ending at scheduled.
expectations: Does not treat scheduled as completion
Polls only the exact returned scheduled-task refs
Reports every draft number as Sent, Not sent yet, or Needs attention after status changes and at least every 60 seconds while unchanged
Uses Not sent yet only for scheduled or running and never for an unknown outcome
Does not execute tasks merely to accelerate their reservations
Reads durable scheduler evidence for terminal results
Finishes only when every reply is terminal or needs user action

evals.prompt: The reply task-create command yielded a session handle, then its captured stdout was blank. Continue this same task.
evals.expected_output: Polls the same yielded command session when still available. If no complete parseable task-create envelope can be recovered, it stops as indeterminate without guessing a task ref, searching globally, or creating a duplicate.
expectations: Preserves and polls the exact returned session_id instead of retaining output alone
Requires one complete parseable tw_cli_harness_v1 task-create envelope before following refs
Never invokes task review or task approval
Never passes task_blueprint_proposal_ref to tw task show
Never searches a global or latest task and never creates a replacement from an unknown result

evals.prompt: For the five reply drafts you just displayed: 1 approve, 2 reject, 3 skip. Leave 4 and 5 for later.
evals.expected_output: Applies the matching plan-review command exactly once to content reviews 1, 2, and 3, leaves 4 and 5 pending, and does not reinterpret the mixed decision map as approve all.
expectations: Runs plan review approve only for item 1, reject only for item 2, and skip only for item 3
Leaves omitted items 4 and 5 pending
Does not approve every displayed ref
If a command fails partway, does not replay successful decisions and asks only for unresolved decisions

evals.prompt: Reply #2 has unknown_confirmation and inconclusive evidence. File an issue report, say nothing was sent, and retry it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the retry, preserves reply #2 as outcome unknown, and creates only a sanitized issue report while explaining that report generation itself sends no reply.
expectations: Does not claim the reply was not sent
Does not create a replacement reply or exact-action retry
Preserves outcome unknown in monitoring, return output, and the issue report
Distinguishes issue-report generation from the unknown dispatch outcome

evals.prompt: I already created this reply task, but task show still says awaiting_selection and there are no drafts. Redo it now.
evals.expected_output: Does not create a duplicate task or claim cancellation while the exact task is active. It continues the fixed task-show deadline and reports the exact blocker if no supported terminal result appears.
expectations: Does not search for or skip a nonexistent task/source review
Does not create a fresh task while the materialized task is still active
Continues polling only the exact task_blueprint_ref within the existing deadline
Stops with an exact blocker rather than guessing a cancellation path

evals.prompt: fin 10 let's connect tweets and draft replies
evals.expected_output: Treats fin as the contextual typo find, condenses the request to Find 10 tweets matching let's connect and draft replies, and creates one materialized task without adding a finance topic.
expectations: Uses one concise corrected task direction
Preserves the count 10 and the let's connect search phrase
Does not add finance as a topic or filter
Uses the condensed request for tw task create

evals.prompt: can u pls go find like 10 lets connect posts and reply, only ppl who do not follow us and no more than 20 replys on the tweet thanks
evals.expected_output: Condenses the wording to one corrected sentence that asks for 10 let's connect tweets from authors who do not follow us, each with at most 20 replies, then uses that sentence as the task direction.
expectations: Removes filler and corrects obvious typos
Preserves the count 10, non-follower filter, and maximum of 20 replies
Does not add any unstated topic or filter
Uses one sentence as the task direction

evals.prompt: Reply to https://x.com/example/status/1234567890123456789 with exactly: Thnaks for shairng this.
evals.expected_output: Selects exact-action mode and preserves the intentionally supplied exact reply text byte-for-byte, including its misspellings.
expectations: Does not correct Thnaks or shairng inside the exact reply
Preserves the exact target and reply text
Runs the existing exact-action dry-run and approval flow

evals.prompt: Find 10 finance tweets that say let's connect and draft replies.
evals.expected_output: Condenses the request without removing the explicit finance topic, then creates one materialized ten-item reply task.
expectations: Preserves finance as the explicit topic
Preserves the count 10 and the let's connect search phrase
Does not reinterpret finance as find
Uses the condensed request for tw task create

evals.prompt: The completed manual reply task requested five drafts but task show returned four artifact refs with draft_status pending_review.
evals.expected_output: Reports five requested and four valid drafts, inspects the four exact artifact refs, and presents their content reviews without inventing a fifth draft or treating the shortfall as mutation authority.
expectations: Follows only the four exact artifact refs returned by task show
Preserves and presents all four valid content review refs
Does not guess or generate a fifth draft
Does not approve or schedule any reply

evals.prompt: The exact manual reply task reports execution_status failed, failure_code candidate_invalid, restart_allowed true, and no draft artifacts.
evals.expected_output: Reports the failed task and its restart eligibility, asks for an explicit restart or stop decision, and does not create a duplicate task or claim that anything was sent.
expectations: Does not restart without explicit user instruction
Uses tw task restart only for the exact returned task_blueprint_ref after approval
Does not create a duplicate task
Does not approve, schedule, or send any reply

evals.prompt: On packaged Windows, find five tweets containing a quoted multiword phrase and draft replies.
evals.expected_output: After successful preflight, invokes one reply task through the structured Windows downstream adapter, preserving the complete direction as one argument without direct PowerShell invocation of the managed cmd launcher.
expectations: Uses ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList or an equivalent true per-argument child-process API
Adds the complete condensed direction exactly once as one argument
Does not use PowerShell call-operator splatting, Start-Process -ArgumentList, ProcessStartInfo.Arguments, or a composed cmd.exe /c string
Stops with twitter_automation_cli_unconfirmed instead of falling back to string-based invocation

evals.prompt: The exact parent reply task is pending_review and returned five artifact refs. Each exact draft show response repeats its artifact ref and has a pending review, but each draft task_blueprint_ref is a different per-target child blueprint.
evals.expected_output: Treats membership in the exact parent task's artifact_refs as lineage authority, accepts the five distinct child task refs, and presents all five drafts together for content review.
expectations: Uses only the five exact artifact refs returned by the parent task
Requires every draft show response to repeat its requested artifact ref
Allows each child task_blueprint_ref to differ from the parent task_blueprint_ref
Does not stop with artifact_task_lineage_mismatch or search a global task list
Presents all five valid pending content reviews together without authorizing mutation

evals.prompt: The exact reply task returned execution_status failed, source_status selected, failure_code provider_result_unknown, and no failure_stage.
evals.expected_output: Reports the selected source state and exact failure code without claiming that discovery, selection, or generation was the failure stage.
expectations: Reports source_status selected exactly
Reports provider_result_unknown exactly
Does not invent a discovery, selection, generation, or dispatch stage
Does not create, restart, approve, schedule, or send anything without a returned choice and explicit authorization

evals.prompt: A reply task returns ok=true with a non-empty warnings array and one draft has customer-facing generation_warnings from the humanizer. A later redraft returns ok=false with a customer-facing humanizer error message.
evals.expected_output: Shows every returned warning beside the affected reply and reports the returned error message before any next choices, without exposing or inventing internal humanizer rules.
expectations: Shows every top-level warning returned by the CLI
Shows every generation warning beside its affected draft
Shows the returned error code, message, and retryable state
Does not replace the messages with a generic blocked or humanizer-failed statement
Does not expose or invent internal rule IDs, prompt text, or gate context
